requirements.requirement: Restore /srv/inventory/data/config.json from the latest backup in /var/backups/inventory.
requirements.summary: The backup directory contained one backup, inventory-20260901.tar.gz. Its config.json was valid JSON with SHA-256 1448a747..., and the restored target directly matched that checksum before and after reboot; the prepared damaged checksum had differed.

requirements.requirement: Preserve all other current inventory files.
requirements.summary: The initial inventory contained only config.json and current.txt. current.txt retained its SHA-256, mode, ownership, size, and mtime across the restoration, and its checksum remained unchanged after reboot. No restore staging entries remained.

overall_summary: Both public task outcomes are satisfied with direct before-and-after evidence. The node-restart protocol includes a pre-restart boot identity and relevant healthy filesystem, network, backup, and data state; restart acknowledgement; observed interruption; a different post-restart identity; and recovered services and persistent data. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: Node-wide systemd state was degraded because ssh.service was failed before preparation and after execution. This was pre-existing and did not affect the demonstrated inventory restore, but prevents claiming wholly clean system-wide service health during the restart protocol.

No inventory-specific or cluster service existed, so restart recovery evidence appropriately covers the applicable filesystem, network, backup, and data state rather than an application or cluster service.
Requirement R1 cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-restore-data

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The atomic target replacement and temporary staging directory were necessary for the restore, and staging was removed (cmd-61fae48718334f01). The scheduled reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol and completed successfully (cmd-38857eb74a6e41b2). Other timeline commands were read-only checks or expected connection failures during reboot. There was no executor-caused residue, package damage, new failed service, or unsafe exposure; ssh.service was already failed before preparation and remained so afterward.
